data.title: Hajj and Umrah Ministry Reviews 2026 Achievements in Service Development and Operational Efficiency
data.content:
Jeddah, November 26, 2026, SPA -- The Ministry of Hajj and Umrah reviewed its key achievements and performance indicators for 2026, reflecting the wise leadership's support for serving worshippers. The achievements included developing digital services, facilitating the arrival of Umrah performers, enhancing operational efficiency, improving the pilgrim experience, and promoting innovation and investment in line with Saudi Vision 2030 and the Pilgrim Experience Program.
    The ministry's efforts helped raise pilgrim satisfaction with services during the 1447 AH Hajj season to 93%, according to the National Center for Performance Measurement of Public Agencies (Adaa).
    To facilitate the Umrah journey, the ministry enabled bookings for Umrah and visit packages through global and regional online travel platforms, integrating package search, booking, and visa issuance. It also qualified more than 10,000 overseas travel agents and included the multiple-entry Umrah visa among its facilitation measures, allowing stays of up to 90 days per year.
    The number of companies providing services to pilgrims from abroad increased to 33, up 20%, while the number of enrichment sites in Makkah and Madinah exceeded 90.
    In digital transformation, the Nusuk application surpassed 70 million users worldwide and offers more than 130 digital services. The Hajj e-track also provides over 500 services to facilitate worshippers' journeys.
    More than 286,000 people participated in beneficiary satisfaction programs across more than 56 countries and 150 service providers. Meanwhile, 41 Nusuk Care centers delivered more than 5.7 million services in 11 languages, and satisfaction with the unified number (1966), available in seven languages, reached 90%.
    During the 1447 AH Hajj season, smart sensors and readers recorded more than six billion readings, enabling real-time monitoring of pilgrim movement and crowd flows, supporting decision-making and improving movement between the holy sites.
    The ministry completed the migration of Nusuk systems to cloud computing, achieving 99.99% system availability, accelerating request processing by more than 50%, and reducing costs by 29%.
    The ministry also developed the Comprehensive Awareness Library, containing more than 185 multilingual awareness materials, and prepared 11 prayer areas under the "All of Makkah Is a Sanctuary" initiative, with a capacity exceeding 120,000 worshippers.  In Al-Jouf Region, the Pilgrims' City, covering 12,000 square meters, served more than 18,000 arrivals through the Kingdom's northern land crossings.
    In innovation and entrepreneurship, ministry programs benefited more than 761,000 people, with 263 teams from over 28 countries. The ministry supported 45 companies in developing more than 200 prototypes and empowered entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized enterprises through the Nusuk Business platform.
    These achievements reflect continued progress in developing the Hajj and Umrah system through integration among government entities and the private and nonprofit sectors, investment in modern technologies, and improved service quality, contributing to the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030 to host more pilgrims and Umrah performers and enrich their experience.
    -- SPA
